Sciatica

One rat sciatic-compression experiment reported reduced pain-like behavior after low-level laser treatment; no direct human study was identified in the exact category.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One rat sciatic-compression experiment reported reduced pain-like behavior after low-level laser treatment; no direct human study was identified in the exact category.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Pain > Sciatica category contains one unique experimental publication. It is a rat sciatic-nerve compression model. No human PBM trial, case series, review, or in-vitro/ex-vivo study was listed in the exact indication category.

Human and clinical evidence

No direct human clinical evidence was identified in the exact category. The animal result should not be described as patient pain relief or improved mobility.

Animal evidence

The study used rats with sciatic nerve compression and compared laser-treated animals with controls. PBM reduced pain-like behavior in the model. The experiment provides evidence about responses in this injury model, but does not establish whether the same treatment would change pain or disability in people (Bertolini et al. 2011).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified in the exact category.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The report used an 830-nm near-infrared laser with two tested fluences, 4 and 8 J/cm². Five treatment days began on postoperative day three. The treatment was delivered to a compressed sciatic nerve in an animal model. This intervention and target differ from non-invasive treatment of human back or leg symptoms, and no patient dose or schedule can be inferred from it.

Interpretation

The only evidence is preclinical and limited to behavior in a rat model. Direct evidence about human pain, function, or lasting recovery is absent from the exact category.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The exact category contains one rat experiment and no clinical study. The reported reduction in pain-like behavior is a preclinical outcome and cannot determine symptom relief or function in people with sciatica. Human trials with a sham comparator, defined symptoms, and follow-up are needed before judging clinical effectiveness.
